name_en: Wat Phra Mahathat Woramahawihan, Nakhon Si Thammarat
name_fr: Wat Phra Mahathat Woramahawihan, Nakhon Si Thammarat
name_es: Wat Phra Mahathat Woramahawihan, Nakhon Si Thammarat
name_ar: وات فرا ماهاتات ووراماهاويهان، محافظة ناخون سي تامارات
short_description_en: Wat Phra Mahathat Woramahawihan (or Phra Mahathat monastery), located in Nakhon Si Thammarat Province in Peninsular Thailand on a narrow ridge between the Pacific and Indian oceans, has served as a major regional Buddhist centre since its founding in the 8th century. Benefiting from the transoceanic trade networks, the monastery was influenced by various religious and architectural traditions including Brahmanism, Hinduism, Mahayana Buddhism and Theravada Buddhism from northeastern India, central Java, Sri Lanka and the Mon region of southern Myanmar. These influences have been integrated into its religious buildings, rituals and cultural traditions. Its distinctive artistic and architectural expressions have exerted a wide-ranging and enduring influence throughout Thailand and across Southeast Asia. The religious and local traditions have continued at the monastery for more than 1,500 years, including the Nakhon Si Thammarat chronicle tradition, the annual cloth-wrapping ceremony for the Great Reliquary and the Nora dance drama.
short_description_fr: Le Wat Phra Mahathat Woramahawihan (ou monastère de Phra Mahathat), situé dans la province de Nakhon Si Thammarat, dans la péninsule thaïlandaise, sur une étroite bande de terre entre les océans Pacifique et Indien, constitue un important centre bouddhique régional depuis sa fondation au VIIIe siècle. Bénéficiant des réseaux d’échanges transocéaniques, le monastère a été influencé par diverses traditions religieuses et architecturales, notamment l’hindouisme, le bouddhisme mahāyāna et le bouddhisme theravāda provenant du nord-est de l’Inde, du centre de Java, du Sri Lanka et de la région môn du sud du Myanmar. Ces influences ont été intégrées à ses édifices religieux, à ses rituels et à ses traditions culturelles. Ses expressions artistiques et architecturales distinctives ont exercé une influence vaste et durable à travers la Thaïlande et l’ensemble de l’Asie du Sud-Est. Les traditions religieuses et locales se sont maintenues au sein du monastère pendant plus de 1 500 ans, notamment la tradition des chroniques de Nakhon Si Thammarat, la cérémonie annuelle d’enveloppement en étoffe du Grand Reliquaire ainsi que le drame dansé Nora.
short_description_es: Wat Phra Mahathat Woramahawihan (o monasterio de Phra Mahathat), situado en la provincia de Nakhon Si Thammarat en Tailandia peninsular, en una estrecha cresta entre los océanos Pacífico e Índico, ha funcionado como un importante centro budista regional desde su fundación en el siglo VIII. El monasterio recibió las influencias de las redes comerciales transoceánicas y de diversas tradiciones religiosas y arquitectónicas como el hinduismo, el budismo mahayana y el budismo theravada del noreste de la India, el centro de Java, Sri Lanka y la región Mon del sur de Myanmar. Estas características se reflejan en sus edificios religiosos, rituales y tradiciones culturales. Sus distintivas expresiones artísticas y arquitectónicas han ejercido una influencia amplia y duradera en Tailandia y en todo el sudeste asiático. En el monasterio siguen vivas tradiciones religiosas y locales que datan de más de 1500 años, como la tradición de la crónica de Nakhon Si Thammarat, la ceremonia anual de envoltura de tela para el Gran Relicario y el drama de danza Nora.
short_description_ru: Ват-Пхра-Махатхат-Ворамахавихан, или монастырь Пхра-Махатхат, расположен в провинции Накхонситхаммарат в полуостровной части Таиланда на узком хребте между Тихим и Индийским океанами. С момента своего основания в VIII веке он был важным буддийским центром региона. Благодаря трансокеанским торговым связям монастырь оказался под влиянием различных религиозных и архитектурных традиций: индуизма, буддизма Махаяны и буддизма Тхеравады, пришедших из северо-восточной Индии, Центральной Явы, Шри-Ланки и региона Мон в южной части Мьянмы. Эти влияния отразились в его культовых зданиях, обрядах и культурных традициях. Самобытные художественные и архитектурные решения монастыря оказали широкое и долговременное влияние на Таиланд и Юго-Восточную Азию. Более 1500 лет здесь сохраняются религиозные и местные традиции, включая традицию хроник Накхонситхаммарата, ежегодную церемонию обертывания тканью Великого реликвария и танцевальную драму нора.
short_description_ar: يقع وات فرا ماهاتات ووراماهاويهان (أو دير فرا ماهاتات) في محافظة ناخون سي تامارات في شبه الجزيرة الجنوبية على سلسلة جبال ضيقة بين المحيط الهادي والمحيط الهندي، وكان مركزاً بوذياً إقليمياً رئيسياً منذ إنشائه في القرن الثامن. وقد استفاد الدير من الشبكات التجارية العابرة للمحيطات، فتأثر بتقاليد دينية ومعمارية متنوعة، تشمل الهندوسية ومذهبَي مهايانا وتيرافادا البوذيَين من شمال شرق الهند ووسط جزيرة جاوة وسري لانكا وولاية مون في جنوب ميانمار. وقد دُمجت هذه التأثيرات في المباني والطقوس الدينية والتقاليد الثقافية. وقد أثَّرت أشكال التعبير الفني والمعماري المميزة لهذا الدير تأثيراً دائماً وواسع النطاق في مختلف أنحاء تايلاند وعبر جنوب شرق آسيا. واستمرت ممارسة التقاليد الدينية والمحلية في الدير لأكثر من 1500 عام، بما فيها تقليد تدوين سجلات ناخون سي تامارات، والحفل السنوي لتغليف صندوق الذخائر العظيم بالقماش، ومسرحية نورا الراقصة.
short_description_zh: 帕玛哈泰沃拉玛哈维汉寺（Wat Phra Mahathat Woramahawihan，又称玛哈泰寺）位于泰国半岛地区的洛坤府，这里是太平洋和印度洋之间的狭长地峡。自8世纪创建以来，该寺一直是重要的区域佛教中心。寺院依托跨洋贸易网络，吸收来自印度东北部、中爪哇、斯里兰卡、缅甸南部孟族地区的印度教、大乘佛教、上座部佛教等多种宗教和建筑传统，并将之融汇于宗教建筑、宗教仪式和文化传统中。其独具特色的艺术与建筑表达对泰国乃至整个东南亚产生了广泛而持久的影响。1500多年来，寺院始终延续着丰富的宗教和地方传统，包括洛坤编年史传统、年度赠僧布围金塔仪式、诺拉舞剧等。
description_en: Wat Phra Mahathat Woramahawihan (or Phra Mahathat monastery), located in Nakhon Si Thammarat Province in Peninsular Thailand on a narrow ridge between the Pacific and Indian oceans, has served as a major regional Buddhist centre since its founding in the 8th century. Benefiting from the transoceanic trade networks, the monastery was influenced by various religious and architectural traditions including Brahmanism, Hinduism, Mahayana Buddhism and Theravada Buddhism from northeastern India, central Java, Sri Lanka and the Mon region of southern Myanmar. These influences have been integrated into its religious buildings, rituals and cultural traditions. Its distinctive artistic and architectural expressions have exerted a wide-ranging and enduring influence throughout Thailand and across Southeast Asia. The religious and local traditions have continued at the monastery for more than 1,500 years, including the Nakhon Si Thammarat chronicle tradition, the annual cloth-wrapping ceremony for the Great Reliquary and the Nora dance drama.
justification_en: Brief synthesis Wat Phra Mahathat Woramahawihan (or Phra Mahathat monastery) is a Theravada Buddhist monastery located in the Nakhon Si Thammarat Province in Peninsular Thailand, a crucial trade crossroad between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Founded in the 8th century, where a Hindu shrine once stood (5th-8th centuries), the monastery has been a regional religious centre ever since. The complex is centred on the Great Reliquary of Buddha in the form of a mandala (Buddhavasa), flanked by the residential quarters of the monks (Sanghavasa) to the north and south according to the Tipiṭaka (Pali Canon). It comprises religious buildings, including the Great Reliquary with satellite stupas, various functional structures, two Bodhi tree shrines and the sacred Crystal Beach, on which the monastery is built, as well as residential buildings in the monastery. Bearing witness to the fusion of Brahmanism, Hinduism and the Mahayana and Theravada Buddhism of South and Southeast Asia, the combined artistic and architectural expressions found at Wat Phra Mahathat, imbued with local and religious traditions, had a lasting influence on building construction in the region. Criterion (ii): Wat Phra Mahathat is an exceptional testament to the interchange of human values. The Great Reliquary demonstrates the influence of Brahmanism, Hinduism and the Mahayana and Theravada schools of Buddhism, originating from Pala art in Nalanda, Central Javanese art, Sri Lankan art and Mon art from southern Myanmar. In turn, the combined architectural style of the Great Reliquary has exerted a profound influence on subsequent religious buildings in Thailand, Malaysia and beyond. Criterion (vi): As the testimony to diverse belief systems and the spiritual centre of Nakhon Si Thammarat, Wat Phra Mahathat is the heart of living religious traditions with artistic and literary works of outstanding universal significance, such as the Nora dance drama and the local chronicles. These traditions vividly represent the relationships between this sacred site and its surrounding communities and inspired other monasteries and communities in Thailand and beyond. Integrity The boundaries of the property follow the outline of Wat Phra Mahathat, which is large enough to include all the attributes conveying the Outstanding Universal Value. The mandala plan of the Great Reliquary complex, the Tipikata layout of the monastery, all the religious buildings and the Crystal Beach on which the monastery was established, are all included in the property. Important views and settings are protected by the buffer zone. The property is in a good state of conservation, and well-maintained by the monastery and local communities, as well as relevant authorities. The modern urban development has no negative impact on the area inside the monastery, and all factors affecting the property are under control. Authenticity The property retains a high level of authenticity in terms of location, function, form, materials, traditions, and spirit. The location and function of the monastery remain unchanged since its establishment in the 8th century. The layouts of the Great Reliquary and the monastery have been authentically preserved. The forms and traces of architectural and artistic expressions of different origins since the 8th century have been preserved at the Great Reliquary stupa. Traditional materials and techniques have been used in the past restorations, which preserved the original forms of religious buildings. The living Bodhi trees testify to the authentic roots of their origin. The sacred sand ground is still preserved. The Phra Mahathat Monastery is still active, continuing its associated traditions. Protection and management requirements The property is inscribed on the List of National Ancient Monuments and has been registered in the Royal Gazette in 1936 and 2024. It is protected under the Act on Ancient Monuments, Antiques, Objects of Art and National Museums (currently under revision) and the Sangha Act, which both provide the highest level of protection at the national level. The buffer zone covers the important views and settings and is protected by a comprehensive framework of legislations and planning regulations at the provincial and municipality levels. Within the buffer zone, a height control zone has been demarcated for protecting the important views. The management framework comprises institutions from national, provincial and municipal levels, and is featured by a combination of traditional and State management, with active participation of local communities. The management activities are guided by the Management Plan of Wat Phra Mahathat (2026-2030) and are supported by the Disaster and Human-Induced Risk Management Plan for the Cultural World Heritage Site, Wat Phra Mahathat Woramahawihan, Nakhon Si Thammarat Province, Thailand, as well as Tourism Management Plan for the Conservation of Cultural Heritage: Wat Phra Mahathat Woramahawihan (2026-2030) developed specially for the monastery.

name_en: Tashkent Modernist Architecture. Modernity and Tradition in Central Asia
name_fr: Architecture moderniste de Tachkent. Modernité et tradition en Asie centrale
name_es: Arquitectura modernista de Tashkent. Modernidad y tradición en Asia Central
name_ru: Модернистская архитектура Ташкента. Современность и традиция в Центральной Азии
name_zh: 塔什干现代主义建筑：中亚的现代性和传统
short_description_en: The property embodies a representative ensemble of ten modernist buildings and urban complexes constructed between the 1960s and early 1990s, a formative period in the reconstruction and transformation of Tashkent following the 1966 earthquake. The series includes museums, exhibition halls, residential ensembles, cultural institutions, and scientific or infrastructural facilities, reflecting the broad functional spectrum of late‑Soviet architectural production. Nine out of ten component parts are situated along the newly planned urban axes of the reconstructed city centre, as defined in successive masterplans that reshaped Tashkent into a modern socialist metropolis. Together, they articulate the city’s principal public spaces and demonstrate the integration of modernist planning principles with local climatic, seismic, and cultural conditions. Collectively, the serial property illustrates a distinct phase of architectural modernism characterised by industrialised construction, seismic‑resilient engineering, and the adaptation of standardised systems to regional materials, traditions, and environmental constraints.
short_description_fr: Le bien présente un ensemble représentatif de dix édifices et ensembles urbains modernistes construits entre les années 1960 et le début des années 1990, une période déterminante dans la reconstruction et la transformation de Tachkent à la suite du séisme de 1966. La série comprend des musées, des halls d’exposition, des ensembles résidentiels, des institutions culturelles ainsi que des équipements scientifiques et d’infrastructure, reflétant le large éventail fonctionnel de la production architecturale soviétique tardive. Neuf des dix éléments constitutifs sont situés le long des nouveaux axes urbains planifiés du centre-ville reconstruit, tels qu’ils ont été définis par les plans directeurs successifs qui ont remodelé Tachkent en une métropole socialiste moderne. Ensemble, ils structurent les principaux espaces publics de la ville et témoignent de l’intégration des principes de l’urbanisme moderniste aux conditions climatiques, sismiques et culturelles locales. Dans son ensemble, le bien en série illustre une phase distinctive du modernisme architectural, caractérisée par la construction industrialisée, l’ingénierie parasismique et l’adaptation de systèmes standardisés aux matériaux régionaux, aux traditions locales et aux contraintes environnementales.
short_description_es: El bien es un conjunto representativo de diez edificios modernistas y complejos urbanos construidos entre la década de 1960 y principios de la década de 1990, un período marcado por la reconstrucción y transformación de Tashkent tras el terremoto de 1966. La serie incluye museos, salas de exposiciones, edificios residenciales, instituciones culturales, instalaciones científicas y otras infraestructuras que reflejan el amplio espectro funcional de la arquitectura soviética tardía. Nueve de los diez elementos están situados a lo largo de los nuevos ejes urbanos del centro de la ciudad reconstruida, como se definió en sucesivos planes urbanos que trasformaron Tashkent en una metrópolis socialista moderna. El conjunto articula los principales espacios públicos de la ciudad y constituye una buena muestra de la integración de los principios de planificación modernista con las condiciones climáticas, sísmicas y culturales locales. Este bien muestra una fase distinta del modernismo arquitectónico caracterizado por la construcción industrializada, la ingeniería sísmica resiliente y la adaptación de sistemas estandarizados a materiales regionales, tradiciones y exigencias ambientales.
short_description_ru: Объект представляет собой ансамбль из десяти модернистских зданий и городских комплексов, построенных с 1960-х до начала 1990-х годов. Этот период стал ключевым для реконструкции и преобразования Ташкента после землетрясения 1966 года. В состав объекта входят музеи, выставочные залы, жилые ансамбли, учреждения культуры, научные и инфраструктурные объекты, что отражает широкий функциональный спектр позднесоветской архитектуры. Девять из десяти компонентов находятся вдоль новых градостроительных осей реконструированного центра, заданных последовательными генеральными планами, благодаря которым Ташкент был преобразован в современный социалистический мегаполис. Вместе эти объекты формируют основные общественные пространства города и показывают, как модернистские принципы планировки были адаптированы к местным климатическим, сейсмическим и культурным условиям. В целом серийный объект иллюстрирует особую фазу архитектурного модернизма, характеризующуюся индустриализированным строительством, сейсмостойкими инженерными решениями и приспособлением стандартизированных систем к региональным материалам, традициям и экологическим ограничениям.
short_description_zh: 遗产由10处代表性现代主义建筑和城市综合体组成，建于20世纪60-90年代初，即1966年地震后塔什干重建和转型的关键阶段。该系列涵盖博物馆、展厅、住宅群、文化机构、科研和基础设施等，体现苏联晚期建筑的多元功能。其中9处位于重建后新规划的市中心城市轴线上。轴线历经多次城市规划形成，将塔什干塑造为现代社会主义都市。遗产的各组成部分共同界定城市主要公共空间，展现现代主义城市规划理念与当地气候条件、抗震需求、文化特色的有机融合。该系列遗产整体反映建筑现代主义发展的一个独特阶段，其特点为工业化建筑、抗震工程，及针对当地材料、传统、环境限制调整标准化建筑体系。
description_en: The property embodies a representative ensemble of ten modernist buildings and urban complexes constructed between the 1960s and early 1990s, a formative period in the reconstruction and transformation of Tashkent following the 1966 earthquake. The series includes museums, exhibition halls, residential ensembles, cultural institutions, and scientific or infrastructural facilities, reflecting the broad functional spectrum of late‑Soviet architectural production. Nine out of ten component parts are situated along the newly planned urban axes of the reconstructed city centre, as defined in successive masterplans that reshaped Tashkent into a modern socialist metropolis. Together, they articulate the city’s principal public spaces and demonstrate the integration of modernist planning principles with local climatic, seismic, and cultural conditions. Collectively, the serial property illustrates a distinct phase of architectural modernism characterised by industrialised construction, seismic‑resilient engineering, and the adaptation of standardised systems to regional materials, traditions, and environmental constraints.

name_fr: Sites de l’industrie de la porcelaine artisanale de Jingdezhen
name_es: Sitios de producción de porcelana artesanal de Jingdezhen
name_ar: مواقع صناعة الخزف التقليدية في جينغدتشن
short_description_en: The serial property portrays the evolution of the production of handicraft porcelain from the 10th to 19th centuries that had profound industrial, artistic and trading influences in China and beyond globally. The five component parts reflect the processes of the production of porcelain, including the extraction and transportation of raw materials, innovations in kiln design and the spatial and social organisation of production on an immense scale. The town area featured the Imperial Kiln alongside civilian kilns, guilds and merchant associations. Jingdezhen was a centre of technological innovation in porcelain production, including the “binary formula” of mixing kaolin and porcelain stone. Porcelain of the highest quality was produced at Jingdezhen, and its blue-and-white porcelain and designs became a prized global commodity and a symbol of Chinese culture and artistry.
short_description_fr: Le bien en série retrace l'évolution, du Xe au XIXe siècle, de la production de porcelaine artisanale, qui eut une influence considérable sur les industries, les arts et le commerce en Chine et dans le monde. Ses cinq éléments constitutifs illustrent les processus de production de la porcelaine, notamment l'extraction et le transport de matières premières, des innovations dans la conception des fours et dans l'organisation spatiale et sociale de la production à très grande échelle. La ville disposait d'un four impérial à côté de fours privés, de corporations et d'associations de marchands. Jingdezhen a été un centre d'innovations technologiques dans la production de porcelaine, parmi lesquelles la « formule binaire » consistant à mélanger du kaolin et de la pierre de porcelaine. Une porcelaine de la plus haute qualité a été produite à Jingdezhen, et sa porcelaine bleu et blanc ainsi que ses motifs sont devenus une marchandise prisée dans le monde et un symbole de la culture et du talent artistique chinois.
short_description_es: El bien en serie retrata la evolución de la producción de porcelana artesanal de los siglos X al XIX con profundas influencias industriales, artísticas y comerciales tanto en China como en el resto del mundo. Los cinco elementos que lo componen representan los procesos de producción de la porcelana, que van desde la extracción y transporte de materias primas, innovaciones en el diseño de hornos, y la organización espacial y social de la producción a gran escala. En la ciudad se encontraban el Horno Imperial, los hornos civiles, gremios y asociaciones de comerciantes. Jingdezhen fue un centro de innovación tecnológica en la producción de porcelana que incluía la «fórmula binaria», mezcla de caolín y piedra de porcelana. En Jingdezhen se producía la porcelana de la más alta calidad, y sus piezas de color azul y blanco, junto con sus diseños, se convirtieron en una mercancía mundial preciada y símbolo de la cultura y el arte chinos.
short_description_ru: Этот серийный объект отражает развитие ремесленного производства фарфора с X по XIX век, оказавшего глубокое влияние на промышленность, искусство и торговлю как в Китае, так и за его пределами. Пять компонентов объекта отражают основные этапы производства фарфора: добычу и транспортировку сырья, новаторские решения в конструкции печей, а также пространственную и социальную организацию производства в огромных масштабах. В городской части находились Императорская печь, гражданские печи, гильдии и торговые объединения. Цзиндэчжэнь был центром технологических инноваций в производстве фарфора, включая «двухкомпонентную формулу» смешивания каолина и фарфорового камня. Здесь производили фарфор высочайшего качества, а бело-синий фарфор Цзиндэчжэня и его орнаменты стали ценным товаром мирового значения и символом китайской культуры и художественного мастерства.
short_description_ar: عتبر الموقع المتسلسل شاهداً على مسيرة تطور صناعة الخزف اليدوي خلال الفترة الممتدة من القرن العاشر إلى القرن التاسع عشر، وما كان لها من أثر بالغ في ازدهار الصناعة والفنون والتجارة، داخل الصين وخارجها. ويتألف الموقع من خمسة عناصر رئيسة تؤرخ مراحل صناعة الخزف، بدءاً باستخراج المواد الخام ونقلها، ومروراً بما شهدته الأفران من تطور وابتكار في تصميمها، وانتهاء بالتنظيم المكاني والاجتماعي الذي قامت عليه عمليات الإنتاج واسعة النطاق.وتضم المنطقة الحضرية الفرن الإمبراطوري إلى جانب الأفران الأهلية، ونقابات الحرفيين، وروابط التجار. وغدت جينغدتشن مركزاً رائداً للابتكار التقني في صناعة الخزف، وتتمثل أبرز إنجازاتها في تطوير الصيغة الثنائية القائمة على مزج الكاولين بحجر الخزف، وهو ابتكار أفضى إلى إنتاج خزف استثنائي الجودة. وسرعان ما ذاع صيت خزف جينغدتشن، ولا سيما الخزف الأبيض الموشح باللون الأزرق، فانتشر في الأسواق العالمية، وغدا سلعة نفيسة ورمزاً للفنون والثقافة الصينية.
short_description_zh: 该系列遗产展示了景德镇10-19世纪手工制瓷业的发展历程，其对中国乃至世界制瓷产业、技术、艺术和贸易产生了深远影响。遗产由5个部分组成，完整体现从原料开采加工到制瓷生产的全过程；以及大规模、集约化生产活动在空间和社会层面的组织方式。瓷业生产中心既有御窑，也有民窑，同时还有行业会馆、祠庙等瓷业社会组织。景德镇还是制瓷技术的重要创新中心，创烧出青花瓷、粉彩瓷等新品类，并发展出高岭土与瓷石混合使用的“二元配方”工艺。景德镇出产品质卓越的瓷器，特别是青花瓷及纹样享誉全球，其艺术风格在世界各地受到研究和仿效，也是中华文化与艺术的重要象征。
description_en: The serial property portrays the evolution of the production of handicraft porcelain from the 10th to 19th centuries that had profound industrial, artistic and trading influences in China and beyond globally. The five component parts reflect the processes of the production of porcelain, including the extraction and transportation of raw materials, innovations in kiln design and the spatial and social organisation of production on an immense scale. The town area featured the Imperial Kiln alongside civilian kilns, guilds and merchant associations. Jingdezhen was a centre of technological innovation in porcelain production, including the “binary formula” of mixing kaolin and porcelain stone. Porcelain of the highest quality was produced at Jingdezhen, and its blue-and-white porcelain and designs became a prized global commodity and a symbol of Chinese culture and artistry.
justification_en: Brief synthesis The Jingdezhen Handicraft Porcelain Industry Sites are located in an area with rich reserves of porcelain stone, kaolin clay, firewood forests and water transportation. Five component parts represent the handicraft porcelain industry system of Jingdezhen from the 10th to the 19th century. Together they exhibit the innovative development of Chinese porcelain making technology and porcelain art that had a profound impact on the development of the ceramic industry of the world. From the 10th to the 13th centuries integration of the porcelain-making technologies of northern and southern China achieved the stable production of bluish-white porcelain and laid the foundation for Jingdezhen to develop into a Chinese porcelain production centre. In the 13th-15th centuries, innovations included the “binary formula” (mixing porcelain stone with kaolin), new kiln forms, and the use of imported cobalt pigments to produce the blue-and-white porcelain. From the 16th century, Jingdezhen was the handicraft porcelain production centre of the world, supported by a complex industrial structure that connected porcelain manufacturing and sales centres with raw material and firewood production areas via a waterway transportation system. The Jingdezhen Handicraft Porcelain Industry Sites bear witness to the formation of a large-scale intensive production model characterised by an industrial chain with fine divisions of labour, standardisation and specialisation, leading to a capacity for high quality porcelain. Through the advancement of production technologies and industrial organisation, Jingdezhen maintained its position as the porcelain production centre of the world from the 16th century, promoting the widespread dissemination of Chinese porcelain making technology, art and products around the world. Criterion (ii): The Jingdezhen Handicraft Porcelain Industry Sites demonstrate global exchanges in porcelain-making technologies and art, and innovations in porcelain production from the 10th to the 19th centuries. The Hutian Ancient Kiln Site portrays the integration of porcelain-making technologies for bluish-white porcelain from the north and south of China from the 10th-13th centuries. The development of technologies at Jingdezhen during the 13th-19th centuries combined traditional Chinese porcelain-making with Middle Eastern, Chinese and European pigments, and a fusion of Chinese and foreign decorative techniques to produce blue-and-white, enamel and famille-rose porcelain. The “binary formula” technology attracted widespread attention and was an important inspiration and influence on the development of high-temperature hard-paste porcelain technology in Europe during the 18th century. Jingdezhen became a world porcelain production centre from the 16th-18th centuries, with its artistic styles studied and imitated all over the world. Criterion (iii): The Jingdezhen Handicraft Porcelain Industry Sites exhibit the continuous production process of the porcelain industry from the 10th to the 19th centuries and a complete industrial pattern including the social organisation of production. The five component parts provide a testimony to the tradition of Chinese handicraft porcelain industry. Criterion (iv): The Jingdezhen Handicraft Porcelain Industry Sites are a technological ensemble that illustrates important stages in the development of the handicraft porcelain industry, an outstanding example of innovation in global porcelain technologies, art and industrial organisation from the 13th to the 19th centuries. The uses of raw materials at Jingdezhen, the “binary formula” technology, modelling technologies, kiln designs, and innovations in underglaze and overglaze decoration techniques enriched the diversity of porcelain shapes and decorative styles. The large-scale industrial spatial layout, division of labour, and specialised and standardised production model enabled the efficient and high-quality porcelain production at Jingdezhen. Criterion (vi): As an important vehicle of Chinese culture and an important symbol of Oriental art, evidence of blue-and-white porcelain of Jingdezhen establishes a direct association with European decorative art from the 17th-18th centuries. As a global high-end trade commodity, the blue-and-white porcelain of Jingdezhen is one of the core elements of “chinoiserie” that was popular in Europe. These artistic elements were widely collected and used in pattern design, painting, furniture, architectural decoration and other fields, with porcelain serving as a medium to promote the global expression of Chinese culture. Integrity The five component parts include raw material sources, kilns, workshops, transportation and other production facilities that demonstrate the elements and stages of the development of the handicraft porcelain technology of Jingdezhen from the 10th to the 19th century. They include buildings used for the social organisation and management, commercial and trade activities, religious and belief practices, and the porcelain production tools and products of Jingdezhen. The Jingdezhen Handicraft Porcelain Industry Sites include a full suite of relevant attributes of the industrial system of porcelain production including the spatial layouts, production facilities and technological processes, and social organisation. The boundaries are appropriately delineated and ensure the protection of the key attributes. The component parts are generally in a good state of conservation, and potential threats are well identified. Authenticity The attributes include archaeological sites, historic buildings, wharves, mining sites, firewood forests, historic roads, and sections of rivers, as well as intangible cultural heritage practices associated with porcelain production. The scale of the porcelain production centre is verified by a series of kiln sites along the east bank of the Changjiang River and the depth of kiln accumulations in the town area. The spatial layout of the porcelain production centre, raw material and firewood production areas, urban and rural environmental settings, and the historic river sections connecting the component parts demonstrate the organisation of the handicraft porcelain industry of Jingdezhen. The authenticity of the attributes has been established by historical maps and literature, and by past and continuing archaeological and historical research. Porcelain making is still the pillar industry in Jingdezhen with continuing community involvement. Protection and management requirements The protection of the Jingdezhen Handicraft Porcelain Industry Sites is supported by national and provincial laws and regulations, including the Law of the People’s Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics (and its regulations), the Regulations of Jiangxi Province for the Conservation of Cultural Heritage, and the Regulations of Jingdezhen Municipality for the Conservation of Handicraft Porcelain Industry Heritage. The five component parts and their buffer zones are incorporated into the territory spatial planning framework. Intangible cultural heritage elements are safeguarded by the Intangible Cultural Heritage Law of the People’s Republic of China and the Regulations of Jiangxi Province on the Intangible Cultural Heritage. A four-level management framework has been established, consisting of the State, Jiangxi Province, Jingdezhen City, and the Jingdezhen Handicraft Porcelain Industry Heritage Conservation Center. This Center is responsible for the coordinated management of the property. The component parts are managed by the Zhushan District and Changjiang District Cultural Heritage Bureaus, the Jingdezhen Imperial Kiln Institute, the Jingdezhen Ceramic Culture Inheritance and Innovation Center, the Gaoling-Yaoli Scenic and Historic Area Management Committee and Fuliang County Cultural Heritage Bureau. The Conservation Management Plan of the Serial Property of “Jingdezhen Handicraft Porcelain Industry Sites” (2025-2035) identifies objectives and specific activities for the conservation, protection and interpretation of the property, including monitoring and stakeholder coordination, community participation in decision-making processes and capacity building. Heritage Impact Assessment processes are in place for each of the component parts. A research plan is in place, and a number of strategies and measures are implemented to manage congestion at heavily visited sites.

name_en: The system of Italian-style condominio theatres of the 18th and 19th centuries in Central Italy
name_fr: Le système des théâtres à l’italienne en condominio des XVIIIe et XIXe siècles en Italie centrale
name_es: El sistema de teatros en condominio a la italiana de los siglos XVIII y XIX en Italia central
name_ru: Система итальянских театров condominio XVIII и XIX века в Центральной Италии
name_ar: منظومة المسارح الإيطالية ذات نظام الملكية المشتركة
name_zh: 意大利式共管剧院体系
short_description_en: The serial property comprises ten Italian‑style condominio theatres built between the mid‑18th and late 19th centuries across Emilia‑Romagna, Marche, and Umbria in central Italy. Architecturally representative of Neoclassicism with Late Baroque influences, these theatres feature tiered boxes, carefully designed auditoriums for optimal acoustics and visibility, stalls, foyers, ridotti, and historic stage machinery. They embody the innovative “condominio” system, a model of collective ownership and public‑private financing that enabled municipalities and private citizens to collaborate in constructing theatres in small and medium‑sized towns. This system fostered the growth of a widespread cultural network, providing new representational spaces for the emerging bourgeoisie and broadening public access to the performing arts. Located at the heart of historic town centres, these theatres became important civic meeting places, hosting performances and public events and contributing to the formation of public opinion.
short_description_fr: Le bien en série est composé de dix théâtres à l'italienne en condominio, construits environ entre le milieu du XVIIIe siècle et la fin du XIXe siècle, situés dans les régions d'Émilie-Romagne, des Marches et d'Ombrie, en Italie centrale. Architecturalement, ces théâtres sont représentatifs du style de leur époque, principalement le néoclassicisme, avec des influences du baroque tardif. Leur programme architectural comprend des loges superposées et des salles de spectacle conçues pour une acoustique et une visibilité optimale, des parterres, des foyers et des ridotti (salons), ainsi que des machineries scéniques. Ils témoignent d'un nouveau modèle de financement, dit « condominio » : ce système de copropriété et de financement public-privé, associant municipalités et citoyens privés, permit de densifier le réseau des théâtres dans les petites et moyennes villes et de créer des espaces de représentation pour la bourgeoisie émergente, offrant un accès élargi à la culture. Construits au cœur des centres-villes, ces théâtres devinrent un nouveau lieu de rencontre où des manifestations pouvaient avoir lieu, et où l'opinion publique se formait.
short_description_es: El bien es un conjunto de diez teatros en copropiedad de estilo italiano construidos entre mediados del siglo XVIII y finales del siglo XIX en las regiones de Emilia-Romaña, Marcas y Umbría, en el centro de Italia. Con una arquitectura representativa del neoclasicismo con influencias del barroco tardío, estos teatros cuentan con palcos en varios niveles, auditorios cuidadosamente diseñados para una acústica y visibilidad óptimas, plateas, vestíbulos, salas anexas o ridotti y maquinaria escénica histórica. Son un ejemplo del innovador sistema de condominio, una propiedad en condominio con un modelo de financiación público-privado que permitió a municipios y ciudadanos colaborar en la construcción de teatros en ciudades pequeñas y medianas. Este sistema fomentó el desarrollo de una red cultural generalizada, con la creación de nuevos espacios de representación para la burguesía emergente y la ampliación del acceso público a las artes escénicas. Situados en los centros históricos de las ciudades, estos teatros se convirtieron en importantes lugares de reunión donde se organizaban representaciones y eventos públicos que contribuyeron a la formación de la opinión pública.
short_description_ru: Серийный объект охватывает десять театров итальянского типа, построенных по системе condominio с середины XVIII до конца XIX века в центральной Италии — на территории Эмилии-Романьи, Марке и Умбрии. Их архитектура относится к неоклассицизму и несёт в себе влияние позднего барокко. В этих театрах представлены многоярусные ложи, тщательно продуманные зрительные залы с хорошей акустикой и обзорностью, партеры, фойе, ридотти и историческая сценическая техника. Эти театры воплощают новаторскую систему condominio — модель совместного владения и государственно-частного финансирования, благодаря которой муниципалитеты и частные граждане могли вместе строить театры в малых и средних городах. Такая система способствовала развитию широкой культурной сети, создавала новые пространства общественного представительства для формирующейся буржуазии и расширяла доступ публики к сценическим искусствам. Эти театры, расположенные в исторических центрах городов, стали важными гражданскими пространствами, где проходили спектакли, публичные мероприятия и формировалось общественное мнение.
short_description_ar: يتألف هذا الموقع المتسلسل من عشرة مسارح إيطالية الطراز، شُيّدت بين منتصف القرن الثامن عشر وأواخر القرن التاسع عشر في أقاليم إميليا رومانيا، وماركي، وأومبريا في وسط إيطاليا. وتُجسّد هذه المسارح ما استقرّ عليه فنُّ العمارة في ذلك العصر من خصائص الطراز النيوكلاسيكي، وقد امتزجت فيه بقايا التقاليد الباروكية المتأخرة، إذ تضم مقصورات متدرجة، وقاعات عروض أُحسِن تدبيرها ليكتمل فيها صفاءُ السمع وحسنُ الرؤية، إضافة إلى مقاعد الجمهور، والردهات، والقاعات الجانبية، والآلات المسرحية التاريخية. وتعتبر هذه المسارح مثالاً لنمط الكوندومينيو المبتكر، وهو نظام يقوم على الملكية المشتركة والتمويل المتضافر بين القطاعين العام والخاص، وأتاح للبلديات والمواطنين من القطاع الخاص التعاون في تشييد المسارح داخل البلدات الصغيرة والمتوسطة الحجم. وأسهم هذا النظام في نشوء شبكة ثقافية واسعة الانتشار، أتاحت للطبقة البرجوازية الصاعدة فضاءات جديدة للتعبير، ووسّعت نطاق الانتفاع بالفنون الأدائية أمام الجمهور. وشُيّدت هذه المسارح في مواقع محورية في قلب المراكز التاريخية للمدن، فاستحالت فضاءات مدنية مهمة للقاء والتفاعل الاجتماعي، استضافت العروض الفنية والفعاليات العامة، وأسهمت في تشكيل الرأي العام.
short_description_zh: 该系列遗产由十座意大利式“共管剧院”（condominio theatres）组成，它们建于18世纪中叶至19世纪末，分布在意大利中部的艾米利亚-罗马涅、马尔凯、翁布里亚等大区。这些剧院在建筑上呈现新古典主义风格，并融合晚期巴洛克特征，设有分层包厢、经过精心设计以优化音响效果和观演视线的观众厅、池座、门厅、休息厅以及历史悠久的舞台机械设施。它们体现了创新性的共管制度，即公私合资、集体共有的建设模式，使地方政府与普通市民能够合作，在中小城镇兴建剧院。这一制度促进了广泛文化网络的发展，为新兴资产阶级提供新的社会展示空间，并扩大公众接触表演艺术的机会。这些剧院大多位于历史城镇中心，是重要的公共集会场所，不仅举办演出和公共活动，也促进了公共舆论的形成。
description_en: The serial property comprises ten Italian‑style condominio theatres built between the mid‑18th and late 19th centuries across Emilia‑Romagna, Marche, and Umbria in central Italy. Architecturally representative of Neoclassicism with Late Baroque influences, these theatres feature tiered boxes, carefully designed auditoriums for optimal acoustics and visibility, stalls, foyers, ridotti, and historic stage machinery. They embody the innovative “condominio” system, a model of collective ownership and public‑private financing that enabled municipalities and private citizens to collaborate in constructing theatres in small and medium‑sized towns. This system fostered the growth of a widespread cultural network, providing new representational spaces for the emerging bourgeoisie and broadening public access to the performing arts. Located at the heart of historic town centres, these theatres became important civic meeting places, hosting performances and public events and contributing to the formation of public opinion.
justification_en: Brief synthesis The condominio theatre represents a major evolution in the Italian-style theatre model around the mid-18th and late 19th centuries, marking the transition from being a place for aristocratic entertainment to becoming a cultural institution driven by an emerging bourgeoisie. Based on a unique partnership between public bodies and groups of wealthy citizens, known as società condominiali, this economic model is founded on collective ownership and the sharing of costs. This management structure enabled the wide spread of theatres, particularly in small and medium-sized towns in Italy. By making the financers of theatre projects partners in their design, the condominio model turned these theatres into spaces for architectural experimentation and as economic driving forces for these small and medium-sized towns. The condominio model thus fostered the development of specific architectural features manifesting themselves in precise adjustments to social spaces (entrance halls, foyer, ridotto), the standardisation of the tiered boxes, the optimisation of sightlines, the development of separate circulation systems, transforming the theatre into a tool of prestige precisely tailored for its users. This model fostered the emergence of spaces for social life where culture belonged to an emerging bourgeoisie. In addition to their artistic purpose, these theatres have also played a role as centres of political awareness, transforming small and medium-sized towns into dynamic social and cultural centres; a function they still retain today. Criterion (iii): The system of Italian-style condominio theatres of the 18th and 19th centuries in Central Italy bears witness to the rapid development in town centres of a phenomenon that saw widespread expansion in the 19th century in Italy and Europe, followed by Latin America. These theatres, which first appeared in the provinces of Emilia-Romagna, Marche and Umbria from around the mid-18th century on, were one of the few places where groups of representatives of the emerging bourgeoisie, patrons of the theatres, could gather, and where public opinion was formed. These theatres, financed via the società condominiali involving public bodies and private citizens in the construction and management of these spaces, embody the transition from an exclusive private domain to civic institutions accessible to a wide audience. The condominio theatres of the regions of Emilia-Romagna, Marche and Umbria, part of the former Papal States, enabled the development of innovative solutions for theatres, reflecting the participation of different social classes and testifying to the new social hierarchy. The longevity of these theatres, which continue to host a wide variety of cultural events today, bears witness to how deeply they are embedded in local community life. Integrity The ten component parts comprising the serial property include the most emblematic examples of condominio theatres. The component parts share all of the defining features developed during the three historical periods under consideration, from the early 18th to the late 19th centuries. Each of the component parts continues to serve the purpose for which it was originally created. The component parts are in a good general state of conservation and, when conservation works are needed, these are scheduled. Authenticity The serial property meets the conditions of authenticity in terms of form and design, materials, use and function, location and setting. All component parts convey the Outstanding Universal Value of the property through a series of common attributes: the financing model through the società condominiali; the continuity of use; and the physical and spatial features of the Italian-style theatre as codified by condominio theatres. Numerous written and visual sources are able to confirm the authenticity of the theatres of the serial property, providing key information for understanding their history and development. Archival documents, including original plans and those of subsequent restorations demonstrate the care taken with the structures and their decorative elements. Protection and management requirements Responsibility for the protection and management of each of the ten component parts of the serial property lies with the national government, and local, regional and municipal authorities. Each component part is protected by town planning regulations and legislation applicable nationally or locally, as well as by public ownership. The main legislative framework is governed by the Cultural Heritage and Landscape Code; Legislative Decree 42/2004 of 22 January 2004, and law 1089/1939 of 1 June 1939. The management system of the serial property is based on the Memorandum of Understanding established between the Ministry of Culture (MiC) and the three regions and municipalities concerned. This agreement defines the roles and responsibilities of these authorities for the long-term conservation and management of the property.

short_description_en: The property is a picturesque village perched on a promontory overlooking the Mediterranean Sea, harmoniously integrated into the cliff topography. It developed around the tomb of a Sufi master and saint, known as Sidi Bou Saïd, who lived in the 12th-13th centuries. Through its architectural fabric and urban planning in symbiosis with the natural environment, its recognisable aesthetic created by emblematic colours, and a mystic aura associated with the Sufi spirituality that permeates the site, the property brings together geomorphology, architecture, and spirituality. It has long inspired artists and continues to attract visitors seeking spiritual serenity.
short_description_fr: Le bien est un village pittoresque, perché sur un promontoire surplombant la mer Méditerranée et s'intégrant harmonieusement dans la topographie de la falaise. Il se développa autour de la sépulture d'un maître et saint soufi, connu sous le nom de Sidi Bou Saïd, qui vécut aux XIIe et XIIIe siècles. Au travers de son tissu architectural et de son urbanisme en symbiose avec l'environnement naturel, de son esthétique reconnaissable créée par des couleurs emblématiques et de son atmosphère mystique liée à la spiritualité soufie qui imprègne le lieu, le bien réunit géomorphologie, architecture et spiritualité, inspirant des artistes et attirant des personnes en quête de sérénité spirituelle.
short_description_es: El bien es un pintoresco pueblo que se alza sobre un promontorio con vistas al mar Mediterráneo armoniosamente integrado en la topografía del acantilado. Se desarrolló alrededor de la tumba de un maestro y santo sufí, conocido como Sidi Bou Said, que vivió en los siglos XII-XIII. Sus características arquitectónicas y urbanísticas en simbiosis con el entorno natural, su reconocible estética creada por colores emblemáticos y el aura mística asociada a la espiritualidad sufí que impregna el lugar convierten a este bien en una fusión de geomorfología, arquitectura y espiritualidad. Durante mucho tiempo ha inspirado a artistas y sigue atrayendo a visitantes que buscan paz espiritual.
short_description_ru: Объект представляет собой живописную деревню, возвышающуюся на мысе над Средиземным морем и гармонично связанную с рельефом скалистого берега. Она возникла вокруг гробницы суфийского наставника и святого, известного как Сиди-Бу-Саид, который жил в XII–XIII веках. Архитектурная ткань и градостроительная планировка деревни находятся в симбиозе с природным окружением. Её узнаваемая эстетика основана на символических цветах, а мистическая аура связана с суфийской духовностью, пронизывающей это место. Здесь геоморфология местности объединяется с архитектурой и духовностью. На протяжении многих лет деревня вдохновляла художников и сегодня продолжает привлекать посетителей, ищущих духовного спокойствия.
short_description_ar: الموقع عبارة عن قرية خلَّابة قابعة في أعلى منحدر مطلٍّ على البحر الأبيض المتوسط، وهي تندمج بانسجام مع تضاريس الجرف. نشأت هذه القرية في محيط قبر ولي صالح صوفي معروف باسم سيدي بوسعيد، كان قد عاش في القرنين الثاني عشر والثالث عشر. وتجتمع في هذا العنصر التضاريس وفن العمارة والبعد الروحاني، التي تتجسد من خلال نسيجه العمراني والتخطيط الحضري اللذين ينسجمان مع البيئة الطبيعية، ومن خلال منظره الجمالي المميز بألوانه الفريدة، وهالته الصوفية المستمَدة من الروحانية الصوفية التي تتخلل المكان. ولطالما ألهم هذا الموقع الفنانين ولا يزال يستقطب الزوار الساعين خلف السكينة الروحية.
short_description_zh: 该遗产是一座风景如画的村镇，坐落于俯瞰地中海的一处岬角之上，与悬崖地貌和谐相融。村庄围绕12-13世纪苏菲派大师、圣人西迪·布·赛义德（Sidi Bou Saïd）的陵墓发展而成。凭借与自然环境相依共生的建筑构造和聚落布局、由标志性色彩塑造的鲜明美感，以及萦绕于此、源自苏菲主义的神秘氛围，遗产融地貌、建筑、精神信仰为一体，长期启发艺术家，持续吸引寻觅心灵宁静的访客。
description_en: The property is a picturesque village perched on a promontory overlooking the Mediterranean Sea, harmoniously integrated into the cliff topography. It developed around the tomb of a Sufi master and saint, known as Sidi Bou Saïd, who lived in the 12th-13th centuries. Through its architectural fabric and urban planning in symbiosis with the natural environment, its recognisable aesthetic created by emblematic colours, and a mystic aura associated with the Sufi spirituality that permeates the site, the property brings together geomorphology, architecture, and spirituality. It has long inspired artists and continues to attract visitors seeking spiritual serenity.
justification_en: Brief synthesis The Village of Sidi Bou Saïd is located on top of a hill overlooking the Mediterranean Sea, in northern Tunisia. It developed as a sanctuary-village as a result of a process of aggregation around the mausoleum of a Sufi saint – Abou Saïd Khalaf Ibn Yahya El Tamimi El Beji, known as Sidi Bou Saïd – supported by successive ruling dynasties, which, from the 16th century onwards, fostered the sacralisation of the place by associating their political legitimacy with the baraka (blessing) of the saint. The Husainid beys (18th-20th century) consolidated this dynamic by building holiday residences in Sidi Bou Saïd and turning it into an elite resort. The property embodies the encounter between the spiritual power of the saint and the temporal political power. With the religious complex of Sidi Bou Saïd at its heart, the village reflects the traditional Arab-Islamic urban planning around a central place, enriched by the 19th-20th century urban-type residential architecture of the notables. Criterion (iii): The Village of Sidi Bou Saïd represents an exceptional testimony to the tradition of village foundations based on a symbiotic relationship formed between the spiritual authority of a saint and the temporal power of a ruling dynasty. It exemplifies in an exceptional way the phenomenon of sanctuary-villages, fundamental to the social and political history of the Maghreb, that developed as a result of a saint’s prestige which provided religious legitimacy to the sovereign, and the sovereign’s patronage which, in return, ensured the perpetuation and prosperity of the saint's sanctuary and village. Integrity The property includes the entire historic village of Sidi Bou Saïd, within its 1915 boundaries, excluding a few later buildings which break with the traditional architectural style of the place. The urban morphology and the fabric of the village have been well preserved, and the landscape setting remains largely unaltered, except for the introduction of a marina below the southern slope of the promontory. Other limited instances in which the integrity of the property has been compromised and visual aspects of the site negatively affected are mostly reversible. The site suffers dangerously from instability related to its geological nature and environmental factors. Developmental pressures are largely under control, but excessive tourism is a major concern that requires strategic reorganisation, as it shows to negatively affect the character of the property. At present, despite changes in the socio-cultural and economic context of the site, the vivacity of Sufi spiritual practices persists. Authenticity The property has maintained its morphological coherence and its urban fabric has remained largely unchanged, owing to the 1915 Beylical decree, which helped preserve the village and its historical density. Land division occurred sporadically. The construction of the marina at the southern foot of the promontory modified to a small degree the landscape setting of the property. The mystical practices associated with Sufism remain active and the places of religious practices have mostly retained their original function. The identity of the village that has shaped its history and culture has been maintained, though it faces increasing threats posed by tourism. The related economic dynamics have already led to some changes in the use of residences within the village. Protection and management requirements The property is protected by the Beylical decree of 1915 and the decree 85-1246 of 1985, which provide strong controls against the changes to the spatial organisation of the village, as well as to the fabric and aesthetic of its built environment. The National Institute of Heritage under the Ministry of Cultural Affairs oversees the protection of the property through the Archaeological, Historical and Traditional Arts Heritage Code of 1994. The Institute is also the central body responsible for the management and conservation of the site. The Urban Development Plan for the municipality of Sidi Bou Saïd regulates land uses while incorporating provisions for the protection of heritage, in line with the Territorial and Urban Planning Code of 1994. The management plan has been prepared for a pilot phase (until 2027) and will be further developed.

short_description_en: The property consists of two component parts: The Theatro da Paz and the Praça da República in Belém, and the Teatro Amazonas and the Largo de São Sebastião in Manaus. These were built in the States of Pará and Amazonas in Brazil during the Amazonian ‘Golden Age’ as a result of the economic peak of the Rubber Cycle between 1879 and 1912. Inspired by French and European architecture and decorated with motifs evoking the Amazon, these ensembles were designed as symbols of political and urban ambition. Inaugurated in 1878 and 1889, the Theatro da Paz and the Praça da República asserted the strategic role of the city of Belém as a port and State capital and celebrated the Brazilian Republic, while the Teatro Amazonas, inaugurated in 1896, was part of the large-scale urban development of Manaus during the rubber boom and, along with the Largo de São Sebastião, expressed the wealth and prestige of the future capital of the Amazon.
short_description_fr: Le bien est constitué de deux éléments constitutifs : le Theatro da Paz et la Praça da República à Belém, et le Teatro Amazonas et le Largo de São Sebastião à Manaus. Ils furent construits au Brésil, dans les États de Pará et d'Amazonas, durant la « Belle Époque » amazonienne, née de l'apogée économique du cycle du caoutchouc, de 1879 à 1912. Inspirés de l'architecture française et européenne et décorés de motifs évoquant l'Amazonie, ces ensembles furent conçus comme les symboles d'une ambition politique et urbaine. Inaugurés en 1878 et 1889, le Theatro da Paz et la Praça da República affirmèrent le rôle stratégique de la ville de Belém en tant que port et capitale de l'État et célébrèrent la République brésilienne, tandis que le Teatro Amazonas, inauguré en 1896, s'inscrivit dans le cadre du développement urbain à grande échelle de Manaus pendant le boom du caoutchouc et, avec le Largo de São Sebastião, exprima la richesse et le prestige de la future capitale de l'Amazonie.

short_description_en: The serial property is composed of six historic towns which developed from urban nuclei that emerged around at least the 11th century and evolved into city-states around the 14th-15th century. They eventually became the principal urban centres of the sultanates established on the islands of the archipelago of Comoros. With a common hierarchical system of social organisation, based on matrilineal and matrilocal customs, age-group systems, and patrilineal Islamic traditions still alive today, the property showcases insular urban forms and architectural expressions that resulted from cultural exchanges related to migration and Indian Ocean trade networks, embedded in the local social, geographical, and environmental context.
short_description_fr: Le bien en série conserve les vestiges de six villes historiques qui se développèrent à partir de noyaux urbains apparus au moins vers le XIe siècle, et qui évoluèrent en cités-États autour des XIVe et XVe siècles. Elles devinrent finalement les principaux centres urbains des sultanats établis sur les îles de l'archipel des Comores. Doté d'un système hiérarchique commun d'organisation sociale, fondé sur des coutumes matrilinéaires et matrilocales, des systèmes de groupes d'âge et des traditions islamiques patrilinéaires encore vivantes de nos jours, le bien met en valeur des formes urbaines insulaires et des expressions architecturales issues des échanges culturels liés aux migrations et aux réseaux commerciaux de l'océan Indien, ancrées dans le contexte social, géographique et environnemental local.
short_description_es: El bien en serie se compone de seis ciudades históricas que se desarrollaron a partir de núcleos urbanos surgidos alrededor del siglo XI y que se transformaron en ciudades-Estado en torno a los siglos XIV-XV. Con el tiempo se convirtieron en los principales centros urbanos de los sultanatos establecidos en las islas del archipiélago de las Comoras. Con un sistema jerárquico común de organización social basado en costumbres matrilineales y matrilocales, sistemas de grupos de edad y tradiciones islámicas patrilineales que aún perduran hoy en día, el bien muestra características urbanas insulares y expresiones arquitectónicas resultantes de intercambios culturales relacionados con la migración y las redes comerciales del océano Índico, arraigadas en el contexto social, geográfico y del entorno local.
short_description_ru: Серийный объект объединяет шесть исторических городов, истоки которых восходят к ранним городским центрам, возникшим как минимум в XI веке и к XIV–XV векам оформившимся в города-государства. Впоследствии они стали главными городскими центрами султанатов, созданных на островах Коморского архипелага. Объект показывает характерные для островной среды формы городской планировки и архитектурного выражения, сформированные культурными обменами, миграцией и торговыми сетями Индийского океана. Эти формы встроены в местный социальный, географический и природный контекст, в котором до настоящего времени сохраняются иерархическая система социальной организации, матрилинейные и матрилокальные обычаи, системы возрастных групп и патрилинейные исламские традиции.
short_description_ar: يتألف هذا الموقع المتسلسل من ست مدن تاريخية نشأت من نوى عمرانية يعود تاريخها إلى القرن الحادي عشر على أقل تقدير، ثم أخذت تنمو وتتسع حتى غدت، خلال القرنين الرابع عشر والخامس عشر، مدناً مستقلة. وأصبحت هذه المدن المراكز الحضرية الرئيسة للسلطنات التي قامت في أرخبيل جزر القمر. ويجسّد الموقع نظاماً اجتماعياً هرمياً، قام على منظومة راسخة من الأعراف والتقاليد، من أبرزها الانتساب إلى الأم والإقامة في موطنها عقب الزواج، إلى جانب نظام الفئات العمرية، والتقاليد الإسلامية القائمة على الانتساب إلى الأب، وهي جميعها تقاليد لا تزال ماثلة حتى اليوم. ويمثل الموقع نموذجاً متميزاً للعمران والعمارة في البيئات الجزرية، إذ نشأت مدنه وتطورت بفعل ما شهدته المنطقة من هجرات متعاقبة، وما اتصل بها حركة التجارة عبر المحيط الهندي، فامتزجت المؤثرات الوافدة بخصائص البيئة المحلية وأحوالها الجغرافية والاجتماعية والبيئية.
short_description_zh: 该系列遗产由6座历史城镇组成。它们起源于11世纪及之前形成的城市聚落，并于14-15世纪前后逐步发展为城邦。它们后来成为科摩罗群岛各苏丹国的主要城市中心。遗产所体现的社会组织具有共同的等级制度，其基础包括延续至今的母系血缘、从妻居住习俗、年龄等级制度以及父系伊斯兰传统。遗产展示了岛屿城市形态及建筑表现形式，这些特征源于人口迁徙以及印度洋贸易网络所带来的文化交流，并深植于当地社会、地理和自然环境之中。
description_en: The serial property is composed of six historic towns which developed from urban nuclei that emerged around at least the 11th century and evolved into city-states around the 14th-15th century. They eventually became the principal urban centres of the sultanates established on the islands of the archipelago of Comoros. With a common hierarchical system of social organisation, based on matrilineal and matrilocal customs, age-group systems, and patrilineal Islamic traditions still alive today, the property showcases insular urban forms and architectural expressions that resulted from cultural exchanges related to migration and Indian Ocean trade networks, embedded in the local social, geographical, and environmental context.
justification_en: Brief synthesis The serial property comprises the best-preserved parts of six historic cities located on the islands of Ngazidja and Ndzuwani in the Comoros. They developed from urban nuclei that emerged around at least the 11th century and evolved into city-states around the 14th-15th century, becoming eventually the principal urban centres of the sultanates established in the archipelago of Comoros within the framework of the formation of a Muslim elite linked to the Swahili world. This heritage ensemble, encompassing urban, architectural, and intangible elements, reflects the richness and specificity of Swahili cultural tradition within the Comorian island context. The former sultanic medinas have preserved their old urban morphology and fabric, and an exceptional set of traditions and social practices still alive today. Compact fabrics, with centrally organised palaces and public squares (bangwe, mpangahari), stone houses and defensive structures, the medinas showcase insular urban forms and architectural expressions that resulted from cultural exchanges related to migration and Indian Ocean trade networks, while displaying a spatial logic dictated by a hierarchical system of social organisation based on matrilineal and matrilocal customs, age-group systems, and patrilineal Islamic traditions. The Comorian historic cities, though founded upon the same fundamental cultural and social basis, evolved along distinct trajectories shaped by their geographic, political, social and historical contexts. Criterion (iii): The Medinas of the Historic Sultanates of the Comoros provide an exceptional testimony to the living cultural traditions and social practices of the Comorian archipelago, which, due to its location and complex history, has become a crossroads for peoples of different origins, between Africa, the Arab world, and Europe, connected by the Indian Ocean. The hierarchical social structures of the Comorian society, based on a synthesis of matrilineal and matrilocal customs, age-group system, and patrilineal Islamic traditions, are reflected in the urban organisation of the medinas, which serve as a setting for social life and celebrations that mark the stages of life of men and women, and which in turn give the tangible heritage its meaning. Criterion (iv): The Medinas of the Historic Sultanates of the Comoros constitute a constellation of distinctive responses in architecture and landscape-making that collectively demonstrate the originality of Comorian urban traditions that adapted Arab-Shirazi influences to the local geographic context and combined them with African social structures and models of communal living. Through complementary responses in architecture, artistry, defensive systems, and landscape-making, created within a shared cultural matrix, the component parts showcase the origins and evolution of urbanism in the Comoros, linked to the arrival of Islam, which marked a significant cultural phase in the history of the Indian Ocean region, and illustrates a historical period that witnessed the development of interaction and exchanges between African cultures, the Arab-Muslim world, and various European powers, and the progressive integration of the region into the global maritime context. Integrity While the Comorian medinas of the series share historical and socio-cultural foundations that structure them, the component parts showcase the diversity of architectural, artistic, and planning responses. Each contributes individually to the series through the varying intensities and modalities of external exchanges which, combined with adaptations to specific geographical and insular contexts, generated distinct urban forms and stylistic identities. The component parts include the best-preserved, but sufficiently large, sections of each medina, with the remaining intra-muros areas and some immediate setting comprised within the buffer zones. The serial property retains high integrity in terms of urban morphology, and the system of religious and socio-cultural spaces and centres. However, the oldest built structures (palaces, city walls, historic mosques) are highly vulnerable, with several cases in serious disrepair. The visual interconnections between the cities and the key elements of their natural environment (volcanos, hills, sea), the geographic setting and the maritime connection to the cities are elements that are functionally important as a support to the protection of the property. Authenticity The urban morphology and the spirit of the medinas remain strong in all six component parts, and the authenticity of their use and function is also very high. However, the authenticity of the material fabric of the historic cities has been partly compromised, particularly where concrete reconstructions have been carried out. The gradual loss of traditional skills and massive replacement of materials represent serious threats to the authenticity of the serial property. Historically, the intra-muros sections of the medinas have not been drastically transformed or remodelled, but areas outside the city walls were affected in the modern times. The relationship of the urban centres with the sea is not fully preserved today due to modern developments. Moreover, none of the medinas maintained the maritime commercial context that characterised them during the sultanate era. The intangible heritage still structures the historic cities and gives meaning to the public and private spaces within the medinas. The customary system makes them living spaces of civic and moral education. Protection and management requirements The serial property is protected by Law No. 20-033/AU of 2020 on the Protection of Cultural and Natural Heritage in the Union of the Comoros, promulgated by Presidential Decree no. 21-013/PR. The development within the component parts is regulated by the Urban Planning and Housing Code of 1986, revised in 2011 by Law no. 11-026 on Urban Planning and Construction in the Union of the Comoros. Both legislations need to be supplemented with regulatory texts, which are under preparation. The Framework Law of the Environment no. 94-018, amended in 1995, regulates the landscape environment. Customary, religious, and traditional laws also apply in all component parts. The legislative basis for the creation of a national inventory has been instituted by the establishment of the National Commission for the Protection of Cultural Heritage (CNPPC), responsible for the definition, implementation, and monitoring of the heritage protection policy. This will allow for the registration or listing of the component parts and their enhanced protection at the highest national level, which is yet to be achieved. The National Office for the Valorisation of Heritage (ONVP) is in charge of the mobilisation of funding for the management, valorisation, and tourism promotion. Urban planning instruments (such as Territorial Development Plans (SAT) or Urban Development Plans (PDU)) are either not yet in place or are currently being developed. Four key ministries are involved in the different aspects of management of the serial property: the Ministry of Youth, Employment, Labour, Sports, Arts, and Culture (preservation of historical monuments and sites, their conservation and development); the Ministry of National Education, Teaching, Scientific Research, Training and Professional Integration (scientific research and training); the Ministry of the Environment, responsible for Tourism; and the Ministry of Regional Planning, Urban Development, responsible for Land Affairs and Land Transport. The National Centre for Documentation and Scientific Research (CNDRS), a public scientific and cultural institution, coordinates activities across different stakeholders. The six component parts administratively fall under six municipalities in four prefectures, whose mandate over the serial property is however limited since most of the land is privately owned or is part of the municipal estate. The traditional management system is primarily implemented through the Village Development Committees. The civil society organisations play an active role in the implementation of public policies at the local level and are formally integrated into the management system through the appointment of site managers from among their members. The management plan with an action plan covering the period 2025-2034 is divided into two phases and is being implemented.
